target_customer: Professional filmmakers, studios and brands that want licensed generative video models and tools
problem: Generative video tools were trained on unlicensed data and lacked professional controls, which blocked commercial production use.
business_model: Usage and enterprise licensing of foundation video models via app and API
product_category: Generative video foundation models and creative studio tools

founders.name: Naeem Talukdar
founders.background_notes: YC page bio: raised over 150 million dollars to build world models, angel investor. Prior employers not given.

founders.name: John Thomas
founders.background_notes: YC page bio: ex management consultant at IBM.

technical_complexity.rationale: Training video foundation models is research-grade; a16z notes no public text-to-video models existed at the start of 2023.

defensibility.rationale: Licensed training data and studio partnerships differentiate it, but the model market attracts large funded rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found through 2025; it raised 154 million dollars total by July 2025 per press release.

market_need_then: At the 2021 batch no public text-to-video model existed; the later need came from Hollywood and brands wanting commercially safe generative video.

branding.domain_note: moonvalley.com, with moonvalley.ai used in the 2023 launch

identity.voice_and_tone: bold all-caps headlines, short emphatic lines such as 'No artifacts. No upscaling.'

branding.brand_signature: Marey model name, after the 19th century chronophotography inventor Etienne-Jules Marey, per press coverage
branding.community_and_virality: 2023 beta ran through Discord according to the YC launch post

brand_strength.rationale: Strong film-industry positioning and press around the licensed-data stance, but the company name itself has little independent recognition.

pivots.from: Consumer text-to-video beta on Discord (2023 launch)
pivots.to: Licensed foundation video models for professional film (Marey, 2025)
pivots.why: Not stated in sources opened; press describes the licensed-data positioning

outcome_analysis: Moonvalley raised a 70 million dollar seed in November 2024 and 84 million dollars in July 2025, bringing total reported funding to 154 million dollars, after the 2021-era team behind Draft moved into generative video. Its edge is a licensed-data model sold to filmmakers via a studio partner. It is a large outcome by funding, though revenue and valuation are not public.
notes: Directory says Winter 2021 but the YC launch post is about three years before the 2026 crawl and a press summary says the team previously ran Draft, so the W21 company and today's Moonvalley may have a different history; founding year unclear (sources say 2023 or 2024). Seed and 84M figures come from search result summaries of TechCrunch and Business Wire, not full page reads; the 43M and 53M SEC filings reported by TechCrunch in 2025 probably belong to the same extension and are not separate rounds. Press names more founders (Mateusz Malinowski, Mikolaj Binkowski, Bryn Mooser) from BetaKit and Bessemer pages seen only in search results, so not listed above. Competitor list left empty: only 2023 launch post names image tools (DALL-E, Stable Diffusion, Midjourney) and no source dated near March 2021 was found. No layoffs, lawsuit or acquisition found; one aggregator lists status as acquired, unverified.
